topic.subject: maths
topic.title: Symmetry
topic.scope: line symmetry, lines of symmetry of figures, rotational symmetry, reflection

misconceptions.statement: A shape only has a line of symmetry if it is vertical.
misconceptions.why: Students often associate symmetry with the human body or standing upright.
misconceptions.fix: A line of symmetry can be vertical, horizontal, or diagonal depending on the shape.

probe.question: Does a rectangle have a horizontal line of symmetry?

misconceptions.root_belief: what is familiar is the only truth
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver children's ideas in science

misconceptions.statement: A shape has rotational symmetry only if it rotates 360 degrees.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the full turn with the property of symmetry.
misconceptions.fix: Rotational symmetry exists if a shape looks the same after a turn of less than 360 degrees.

probe.question: Does a square have rotational symmetry?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it only looks the same after a full circle.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: A mirror image is exactly the same as the original object.
misconceptions.why: Students ignore the left-right reversal occurring in mirrors.
misconceptions.fix: Mirror images show lateral inversion, meaning left and right are swapped.

probe.question: If you hold the letter 'P' to a mirror, what do you see?

misconceptions.root_belief: what you see is what is there

misconceptions.statement: A regular polygon has only one line of symmetry.
misconceptions.why: Students fail to count all possible axes of symmetry in complex shapes.
misconceptions.fix: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides.

probe.question: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause

misconceptions.statement: A regular polygon with n sides has fewer than n lines of symmetry, such as a square having only 2.
misconceptions.why: Students count only the obvious horizontal and vertical lines and forget the diagonals.
misconceptions.fix: A regular polygon with n sides has exactly n lines of symmetry. A square has 4: two through midpoints of opposite sides and two diagonals.

probe.question: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

misconceptions.root_belief: Only upright lines count as symmetry lines

misconceptions.statement: A diagonal of a rectangle is a line of symmetry.
misconceptions.why: Students assume any line joining opposite corners divides the shape into two equal halves, and equal area is mistaken for mirror matching.
misconceptions.fix: A line of symmetry must fold the shape so the two halves match exactly. A rectangle's diagonal gives two congruent triangles that do not fold onto each other. A rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry, joining midpoints of opposite sides.

probe.question: How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?

misconceptions.root_belief: Any line that halves a shape is symmetry

misconceptions.statement: The order of rotational symmetry of a shape is the number of its sides.
misconceptions.why: Students generalise from regular polygons, such as the equilateral triangle having order 3, to all shapes.
misconceptions.fix: Order is the number of times a shape looks exactly the same in one full turn. A rectangle has 4 sides but order 2, and a parallelogram also has order 2.

probe.question: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a rectangle?

misconceptions.statement: An irregular shape cannot have any symmetry.
misconceptions.why: Students link symmetry with regular, neat shapes, so irregular means no symmetry.
misconceptions.fix: Irregular shapes can have symmetry. An isosceles triangle has 1 line of symmetry and a kite has 1, though neither is regular.

probe.question: Does an isosceles triangle, which is not regular, have a line of symmetry?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it is not a regular shape

misconceptions.root_belief: Symmetry belongs only to regular shapes

misconceptions.why: Students see two matching pairs of sides and the slanted shape looks balanced.
misconceptions.fix: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle or rhombus has no line of symmetry because folding does not make the halves match. It has rotational symmetry of order 2.

probe.question: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram with unequal adjacent sides and no right angles have?

misconceptions.root_belief: Equal opposite sides means mirror symmetry

misconceptions.statement: The center of rotation can be any point on the shape.
misconceptions.why: Students treat rotating as turning about a corner or any convenient point.
misconceptions.fix: For rotational symmetry the shape must turn about a fixed point, its center. Turning about a different point gives a different position, so the shape may no longer match itself.

probe.question: A square is turned about one corner by 90 degrees. Does it fit exactly on itself?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, any point works as the center

misconceptions.root_belief: Any point can be turning center

misconceptions.statement: A mirror flips an object upside down, so the top and bottom swap.
misconceptions.why: Students recall that text looks reversed and wrongly decide that the mirror turns things upside down.
misconceptions.fix: A vertical mirror swaps left and right, not top and bottom. The image stays upright and only its sides are reversed, so the word AMBULANCE is printed reversed to be read in a rear-view mirror.

probe.question: A word is held in front of a vertical mirror. How does its image look?

misconceptions.statement: A shape with a horizontal line of symmetry must also have a vertical line of symmetry.
misconceptions.why: Students think symmetry lines come as a horizontal and vertical pair, as in a rectangle.
misconceptions.fix: The lines are independent. The letter B has a horizontal line only, and the letter M has a vertical line only.

probe.question: The letter C has a horizontal line of symmetry. Does it have a vertical one too?

misconceptions.root_belief: Symmetry lines always occur in pairs
